FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Thiacloprid technical is employed in the preparation of Insecticide formulations. 
Thiacloprid is the accepted common name by the IUPAC for: 
{(2Z)-3-[(6-Chloropyridin-3-yl)methyl]-1,3-thiazolidin-2-ylidene} cyanamide 


The empirical and structural formula and molecular mass of Thiacloprid are given below: 


Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass 
C10H9CIN4S 252.72 g/mol

and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard 1s complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result ofa test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 
THIACLOPRID, TECHNICAL — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and methods 
of sampling and test for Thiacloprid, technical. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below. 


IS No. Title

their formulations (first revision)

pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides 
(second revision) 

Methods of sampling for technical 
grade pesticides (first revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


8190 (Part 1) : 1988 


10946 : 1996 


3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of light brown powder, 
free from extraneous matter. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 


4 PACKING 


The general requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 1) shall 
be followed. In addition, the material shall be packed 
in multi layered sack with following combination: 


a) Layer wise combination: Inside to Outside 
Inner layer - LDPE ( 50 micron ), three layers 


of paper (70 GSM each), Outermost paper 
(70 GSM) with PE lining (20 GSM) 

or 
Mild Steel drums with LDPE bag inside LDPE 
( 80 micron ) and Mild Steel sheet thickness 
(0.60 mm, Min) 


5 MARKING 
5.1 The sack shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following information in addition to any other 


information as is necessary under /nsecticides Act, 1968 
and Rules framed thereunder: 


b) 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Netquantity; 

g) Nominal Thiacloprid content, percent (m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968, and Rules framed 
thereunder; and 

j) Any other information required under the 


Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the license for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards.

IS 16710 : 2019 


6 SAMPLING 


Representative samples shall be drawn as prescribed 
in IS 10946. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred 
in col 4 and 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in the tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


ANNEX A 
[Clause 3.2, Table 1, SI No. (1)] 
DETERMINATION OF THIACLOPRID CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


A-1.1 Thiacloprid content is determined by High 
Performance Liquid chromatography (HPLC) with 
UV-VIS detector using Internal standard techniques. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 High Performance Liquid chromatograph 
(HPLC) equipped with UV-VIS detector and coupled 
to a printer-cum-integrator. The operative conditions 
suggested below are typical, which can be changed 
provided the standardization is done. 


Column Stainless steel, C-18, 5um, 25 
cm length 4.6 mm ID or 
equivalent 

Mobile Phase Acetonitrile : Water (80 : 20 v/v) 

Flow rate 1.0 ml/min 

Detector UV detector (240 nm) 


Injection volume 20 ul 
A-2.2 Microlitre Syringe — 5 / 20 ul. 


A-2.3 Glasswares 


A-3 REAGEANTS 
A-3.1 Acetonitrile HPLC grade or equivalent. 
A-3.2 Water HPLC grade or equivalent. 


A-3.3 Internal Standard — Acenaphthene AR grade 
or equivalent. 


A-3.4 Thiacloprid Reference Standard, of known 
purity. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Mix acetonitrile and water in the proportion of 80:20 
(v/v) and pass through a membrane filter under vacuum. 
Homogenize the mixture using a magnetic stirrer and 
allow to attain the room temperature. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh out accurately 0.1 g of acenaphthene into a 100 
ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in mobile phase and make 
up the volume up to the mark with mobile phase. Shake 
well to homogenize. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh out accurately 0.1 g of Thiacloprid reference 
standard of known purity into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 20 ml of mobile phase. Keep the flask for 10 min. 
Make up the volume up to the mark with mobile phase 
(Solution A). 


Pipette out 10 ml of solution A in 100 ml volumetric 
flask. Make up the volume up to the mark with mobile 
phase (Solution B). 


Pipette out 10 ml of solution B in 100 ml volumetric 
flask containing 20 ml internal standard (see A-4.2). 
Make up the volume up to the mark with mobile phase 
to 100 ml. Shake well to homogenize. This is a standard 
solution. 


A-4.4 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh out accurately a quantity of a sample equivalent 
to 0.1 g of Thiacloprid into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 20 ml of mobile phase. Keep the flask for 10 min. 


Make up the volume up to the mark with mobile phase 
(Solution C). 


Pipette out 10 ml of solution C in 100 ml volumetric 
flask. Make up the volume up to the mark with mobile 
phase (Solution D). 


Pipette out 10 ml of solution D in 100 ml volumetric 
flask containing 20 ml internal standard (see A-4.2). 
Make up the volume up to the mark with mobile phase 
to 100 ml. Shake well to homogenize. This is a sample 
solution. 


A-4.5 Estimation 


A-4.5.1 Inject 20 pl of reference standard solution 
(see A-4.3) into the HPLC followed by 20 ul of the 
sample solution (see A-4.4). 


From the chromatograms of standard solution and 
sample solution, measure the peak areas of internal 
standard and Thiacloprid peaks and compute the 
percentage of Thiacloprid as given in A-5. 


NOTE — Use guard column for reverse phase and change the 
guard column when the peak shape gets disturbed 


IS 16710 : 2019 


A-4.5.2 Retention Times (Guide Values) 


Thiacloprid — 2.60 min 
Internal standard (Acenaphthene) — 4.00 min 
Total run time — 6.00 min 
A-5 CALCULATIONS 
M,xA,xA,xp 
Thiacloprid content, percent by mass = TM, x4 xA 
where 
M, = mass of standard Thiacloprid in standard 


solution, in g; 

M, = mass ofthe sample taken for test, in g; 

A, = peak area of the Thiacloprid in the 
chromatogram of standard solution; 

A, = peak area of Thiacloprid in the 
chromatogram of sample solution; 

A, = peak area of Internal standard in the 
chromatogram of standard solution; 

A, = peak area of Internal standard in the 
chromatogram of sample solution; and 

p = percent purity of Thiacloprid reference 
standard.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
